text: Eating less salt is a well-known way to help keep blood pressure down.
No headache means your blood pressure is fine.
High blood pressure often feels like nothing at all. Get it checked.
Only old people can have high blood pressure.
Younger adults can have it too. Everyone can get a check.
COUGH CHECK
a cough-check poster
DOH and WHO tuberculosis guidance: a cough of two weeks or more needs a check; TB is curable with full treatment.
Coughing for two weeks? Get checked!
TB can be cured!
Breathe easy, get checked today!
A cough lasting two weeks or more should be checked at the health center.
A long cough can be a sign of TB or something else. A health worker can check.
TB can be cured when treatment is taken all the way to the end.
TB is curable, but only when the full treatment is finished.
A cough that lasts for weeks is normal and will pass.
A cough that lasts for weeks should be checked, not waited out.
You catch TB by sharing a spoon or a plate.
TB spreads through the air when a sick person coughs, not through plates.
SAFE WATER
a safe-drinking-water poster
WHO and DOH safe water guidance: clear water can still carry germs; boil or treat it and store it covered.
Boil it first, then drink!
Clean water, healthy home!
Boil it, cover it, sip it safe!
Boil drinking water, or treat it, when you are not sure it is safe.
Boiling kills the germs that cause stomach illness.
Keep drinking water in a clean, covered container.
A cover keeps dirt, insects and dirty hands out.
Clear water is always safe to drink.
Water can look clear and still carry germs you cannot see.
A pinch of salt makes any water safe.
Salt does not kill the germs in water. Boil or treat it instead.
RABIES ALERT
a rabies-alert poster
WHO and DOH rabies guidance: wash a bite at once, see a health worker, and vaccinate dogs.
Dog bite? Wash it, then get checked!
Vaccinate pets, protect everyone!
Be a good owner, vaccinate your dog!
Wash a dog bite with soap and running water right away, then go to the health center.
Washing at once helps, and a health worker decides what care is needed.
Get your dogs vaccinated against rabies.
Vaccinated dogs cannot pass on rabies, which protects the whole barangay.
Put garlic on a dog bite. There is no need to see a health worker.
Garlic does nothing for rabies. Every bite needs a health worker.
A dog that looks healthy can never give you rabies.
A dog can pass on rabies before it looks sick. Treat every bite seriously.
HEALTHY START
a healthy-start-for-babies poster
WHO and DOH infant feeding guidance: breast milk alone for the first six months, plus regular check-ups.
Mother’s milk, the first gift!
Baby check-ups, never miss one!
Little ones, big futures!
Breast milk alone is the best food for a baby’s first six months.
For the first six months, breast milk gives a baby everything needed.
Take your baby to regular check-ups at the health center.
Check-ups track growth and make sure vaccines are on time.
Babies need rice porridge from the first month.
Other foods can wait until about six months. Ask the health worker.
Babies need extra water in hot months before six months.
Breast milk already has the water a young baby needs.
SPEC M7: label AI-made pictures, ask consent, give credit; facts come from the curated pool in parts.ts
The budget is tiny: use the AI-generated picture.
The captain wants a local face: use Mang Rey’s photo.
The captain wants local art: use Ate Dani’s drawing.
No time to write: use the AI tool’s slogan.
Tasks arrive in a queue at the top. Send each one to the AI lane (left) or to the person (right) before it waits too long.
Tap a task, then tap a lane. Or drag the task onto a lane. With the keyboard: Up and Down choose a task, Left sends it to the AI, Right sends it to the person.
AI is instant at repeat jobs such as counting, sorting, translating a draft and scheduling. It fails at comforting people and at judgement calls.
The person is slow and can hold only three jobs. Giving them a repeat job works, but it wastes the time you need for care.
The Service meter drops when AI fails, when a task waits too long, or when the queue is full. It is empty at zero. Each new day is faster, with a new mix.
Thank goodness you are here!
Welcome to a busy day. Tasks pile up fast, and you decide who does each one: the AI helper or a person.
AI is a fast helper
AI is quick and never tired at repeat jobs: counting stock, sorting lists, drafting, scheduling. Send those to the AI lane.
People do the caring
Comforting a worried mother, a referral, a tricky decision: these need a person. AI fails here, sometimes in funny ways.
Tap a task and then a lane, or drag it there. On a keyboard, use Up and Down, then Left for AI and Right for the person.
Trust AI with repeat drafts you can check. Keep people for care and decisions.
When should I trust it? With repeat drafts I can check. I keep care and decisions for people, and someone is always responsible.
SPEC M6: AI as a tool at work with humans in the loop; health tasks stay general and point to a health worker
KUYA JUN'S CLINIC
Kuya Jun's barangay health work
ALING NENA'S STORE
Aling Nena's corner store
STOCK
Count the boxes of vitamins and masks in the stockroom.
Counting is the same job again and again. AI is fast at it.
Kuya Jun counted every box by hand. The mothers kept waiting.
LEAFLET
Translate the dengue leaflet draft into Hiligaynon.
AI drafts fast. A fluent speaker must check it before it is printed.
It was translated by hand, word by word. It took all day.
VISITS
Plan this week's home visits so nobody is skipped.
Fitting names into days is a pattern job. Check the plan first.
The plan was rubbed out and redone four times. Hours gone.
RECORDS
Sort sixty household records by purok.
Sorting a long list is quick for AI, and easy for you to spot-check.
Sixty cards sorted by hand. The pile was neat, the day was gone.
REPORT
Fill in the monthly report form from the clinic tally sheet.
Copying numbers into a form is repetitive. Read it before you send.
Typed in by hand, number by number. The care work had to wait.
REMIND
Write a reminder text for Saturday's immunization day.
A short, plain reminder is an easy AI draft. You read it and send it.
Half an hour went into the right words for one little text.
TALLY
Add up how many children were weighed this month.
Adding columns of numbers is what computers do best.
The numbers were added by hand, twice, to be sure. Ages!
HOURS
Type up the handwritten clinic hours for the notice board.
Turning handwriting into text is quick, and mistakes are easy to see.
It was copied letter by letter. A person was tied up for ages.
SHEETS
Turn the paper sign-in sheets into one spreadsheet.
Moving rows from paper to a table is repetitive. AI does it in seconds.
Every row was typed by hand. A whole afternoon, gone.
COMFORT
A worried mother is in tears at the door. Comfort her.
Comfort comes from a person who listens. AI cannot feel it.
The AI told the worried mother 'Error 404: comfort not found'.
REFER?
Decide whether a patient should be sent to the hospital today.
A referral is a health decision. A trained worker answers for it.
The AI said 'Refer everybody!' and the hospital line grew long.
Explain to a family that Lolo needs more check-ups.
Hard news needs a gentle voice, a face and time for questions.
The AI sent 'RESULT: ABNORMAL', no hello. The family panicked.
LONELY
Visit Lolo Ben, who lives alone and feels very low.
Being there is the care. A kind face cannot be sent as a message.
The AI sent Lolo a thumbs-up sticker. He asked, 'Who is this?'
WHO 1ST
Two homes need help at once. Who goes first?
You know the families and the roads. That is local knowledge.
The AI sent you to the nearest house. The sicker family waited.
SCARED
A shy teen is scared of her first check-up. Calm her down.
A calm voice and a smile help her trust the check-up.
The AI read her a long leaflet. She hid behind her mother.
REFUSE
A father says no to the vaccine. Listen to his reasons.
Trust grows when you listen. Then share the facts kindly.
The AI replied 'Your opinion is invalid.' The door stayed shut.
NOTICE
At the weighing, a child looks too thin and too quiet.
